text:
marta: Quick sync — proposing a healthscore-driven auto-shed flow for flaky GPUs. Idea: compute a rolling "healthscore" from ECC spikes, XID counts, GPU reboots, and mem ECC logs. If score passes threshold, we soft-cordon + drain non-critical pods (and SLURM/long jobs) with a 10m graceful window. If node stabilizes for 30m, auto-revive. Opening for feedback before I write the RFC.

rajesh: +1 on the concept. Question: how strict are the thresholds? we need hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.

marta: Agreed on hysteresis. Rough thresholds I'm thinking: ECC spikes > 5 in 1h OR XID errors >= 3 in 30m OR GPU-initiated reboot in last 15m = immediate quarantine candidate. But require sustained condition for ~5m to avoid one-offs. Hysteresis: lower bar to mark healthy again (e.g., zero errors for 30m).

oliver: We must not evict Dedicated pools (reserved capacity) or paid customers automatically. Can we make policies per pool/label?

marta: Yes — policy tiers. Default (shared): auto soft-drain. Reserved/dedicated: annotate and page oncall + set node to cordon but do NOT drain until manual approve, unless admin override configured. We'll add a per-cluster config map: `gpu-health.policy` with tiers.

yuna: For SLURM nodes, draining means marking `DOWN` or `DRAIN` via `scontrol update NodeName=... State=DRAIN Reason="gpu-healthscore"`. We should reuse existing `sacct` windows to avoid killing interactive/big jobs.

rajesh: Also propose taint/label scheme: add label `redwood/gpu-health=score:<n>` and taint `redwood/gpu-quarantine=true:NoSchedule`. Use `kubectl annotate` for the short-lived metadata. Example: 
```
kubectl annotate node ip-10-0-2-45 "redwood/gpu-health=score:78" --overwrite
kubectl taint nodes ip-10-0-2-45 redwood/gpu-quarantine=true:NoSchedule --overwrite
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-2-45
kubectl drain ip-10-0-2-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=600
```

oliver: For draining, add a `--force` guard only in emergencies. Also respect pod disruption budgets — our controller should attempt graceful eviction and fall back to marking node for replacement if drain stalls.

marta: Good call. Plan for controller:
- Health collector (prometheus + node exporter plugin) exports ECC/XID counts and last-reboot
- Healthscore service calculates weighted score and writes to etcd/kv + node annotations
- Auto-shed controller reads scores, applies policy map for the node's pool, takes action (taint/cordon/drain or alert)
- Revive controller clears taint/uncordon when stable window observed

sre-bot: Note: Make sure the controller respects cluster autoscaler constraints. If we cordon too many nodes we may break scaling.

marta: Yep — include a guard: `max_percent_quarantined_per_zone` default 5%. Also maintain a soft reserve of spare GPUs to avoid OOM. We'll surface token-level cost impacts in console when draining increases service latency/cost.

rajesh: How do we handle noisy hardware that spikes ECC but recovers? maybe run a local memtest to confirm before drain.

marta: I like that. Proposed action sequence: on threshold crossed -> run quick memtest job (non-destructive light test) and check dmesg for persistent ECC lines. If memtest passes and errors are transient, just annotate and increase sampling. If memtest fails or errors persist, proceed to quarantine.

infra-oncall: FYI: add an automatic incident draft when a dedicated node moves to quarantine so CS can triage customer impact.

yuna: For Slurm, we need a mapping layer: node annotation -> slurm node state. We can use a small adaptor service that watches k8s node annotations and calls `scontrol`.

marta: Example sample logs from collector: 
```
[collector] node=ip-10-0-2-45 ecc_spikes=7 xid_errors=0 reboots=0 temp_c=74 last_seen=2025-11-03T18:02:12Z
[healthscore] node=ip-10-0-2-45 score=82 reason="ecc:7"
[controller] node=ip-10-0-2-45 action=soft-quarantine apply_taint=true cordon=true drain_window=600
```

rajesh: Suggest we can also route low-SLO traffic to cheaper model variants when nodes are lost, instead of immediate scale-up. That helps cost.

marta: Good cross-team note — Redwood Optimize should expose reroute policies we can use as fallback. I'll add an eval in the playbook to measure QPS impact.

deploybot: scheduled job `gpu-healthscore-checker` created: cron @every 1m -> image: redwood/gpu-health:canary (deployed to dev cluster) :white_check_mark:

marta: I'll open the RFC + PR tonight with config schema, playbook, and a canary plan that runs in dev then staging. If you want early review, ping me or comment on the RFC.

oliver: Thanks — will review tomorrow. Make sure to include rollback steps and a manual `unquarantine` endpoint.

marta: Yup. Will include `redwoodctl node unquarantine <node>` and an api to override policy.

rajesh: Also add metric exports for `healthscore_changes_total` and `quarantine_actions_total` for billing/analysis.

marta: Will do. Thanks all :pray:
